entry.name: Anna Maria Island
entry.pitch: A pool house a short walk from the Gulf, on an island where you can bike everywhere and walk the little villages. There are nonstops from all three airports, beach and pool every day for the kids, and Sarasota and St. Petersburg within an hour. No surf though, since the Gulf is usually flat in December.
why: About six hours door to door. Breeze flies Norfolk to Tampa nonstop, Richmond has had the same, and Austin has nonstops to Tampa.
Beach and pool every day for a three-year-old, bikes for a seven-year-old, and Pine Avenue and Bridge Street for the adults.

Sarasota and St. Petersburg are 30 to 60 minutes away, with the Ringling, Selby Gardens' holiday lights (2026 dates still to confirm), the Chihuly Collection (picking up from Mom's July trip) and the Mote aquarium.
A Crystal River manatee snorkel in peak season, about 2 to 2.5 hours up the coast, a boat day to Egmont Key, and mangrove paddles.
catch: No surf, and the Gulf is usually flat in December, so the more active days would be a manatee morning, a boat day and bikes.
Gulf water runs in the mid to upper sixties, so the pool would probably do most of the swimming duty.
The main listing has five true bedrooms plus a den with a bunk and trundle, so we'd want to confirm whether there's a real sixth room.
The big question this late is holiday-week availability on the island. Listed peak rates for six-bedroom houses run $1,755 to $2,251 a night before taxes and fees (checked Oct 21).
There are a few restaurants on the island, but most meals would probably be at the house, maybe with a chef for New Year's Eve.
entry.weather: Highs around 70 to 75, lows in the 50s, Gulf water in the high 60s. Beach and pool weather most days, though a cold front can bring wind.

getting_there.how: Breeze Airways nonstop to Tampa, about 2 hours 15 minutes, then about 1 hour 15 minutes by car to Holmes Beach. Frontier is seasonal.
Breeze flew nonstop to Tampa on last year's schedule, or there's Sarasota on Breeze. The December days still need checking.
Southwest nonstop to Tampa, about 3 a day on weekdays. Delta to Tampa and an Allegiant option to Sarasota (30 minutes from the island) are worth a look too.
Two SUVs for the week, plus bikes on the island.

houses.name: Paradise Beach House, 403 42nd St, Holmes Beach
houses.detail: Three king masters, a queen room, a twin room and a den with a bunk and trundle, every bedroom with its own bath, a heated pool, and a short walk to the beach and shops.
houses.price: Estimate $2,000 to $3,500 a night for the holiday week, unquoted
houses.verdict: Five true bedrooms plus the den. Worth asking for a quote and about the den.

houses.name: Emerald Kite six-bedroom retreat, Holmes Beach
houses.detail: Six bedrooms, five baths, private pool.
houses.price: Listed peak rate $1,755 a night before taxes and fees (checked Oct 21)
houses.verdict: Six bedrooms at the published peak rate.

houses.name: Emerald Kite luxury six-bedroom, Holmes Beach
houses.detail: Six bedrooms, four baths, private pool.
houses.price: Listed peak rate $2,251 a night before taxes and fees (checked Oct 21)
houses.verdict: Six bedrooms, the pricier of the two.

agenda.all: Fly to Tampa, pick up the cars, a Publix run, check in. Pool, then sunset at Bean Point.
An island day with bikes, the beach, Pine Avenue and lunch at The Waterfront.
agenda.relax: A spa slot or the beach. Kids at the beach.

agenda.crew: An early start for the Crystal River manatee snorkel, back mid-afternoon.
agenda.relax: The Mote SEA aquarium in Sarasota with the kids.

agenda.all: Sarasota together, with the Ringling (art, Ca' d'Zan, the circus museum for Bennett), then Selby Gardens' Lights in Bloom after dark (2026 dates still to confirm).
New Year's Eve chef dinner at the house.
agenda.crew: A half-day boat charter for fishing, dolphins and Egmont Key. Maybe wing-foil or kite if a front brings wind.
agenda.relax: Beach, pool, spa. One idea for Mom: a plane checkout at Sarasota and a coastal flight.

agenda.all: A slow beach day, with Patrick taking family photos at golden hour.
A St. Petersburg morning at the Chihuly Collection, a waterfront lunch, back for sunset.
Check out and take the same nonstops home.

pricing.note: Listed peak rates of $1,755 to $2,251 a night at the two Emerald Kite homes, up to the Paradise Beach House guess. No holiday quote yet

entry.name: Asheville
entry.pitch: A six-bedroom house with a hot tub fifteen minutes from downtown, about seven hours of driving from Virginia Beach, or eight to nine with stops. Biltmore at Christmas, the Grove Park spa and gingerbread houses, and maybe skiing at Cataloochee as a bonus rather than the plan.
why: We could drive down, so no airports for nine of the ten of us, and we'd have three family cars for the week.
Biltmore's Candlelight Christmas Evening, Olmsted's gardens, and the Grove Park Inn's National Gingerbread House display.
Posana downtown does steak, short rib and lobster gnocchi.
Hikes and the spa, with a Cataloochee or Sugar Mountain day if the snowmaking holds, and Bent Creek or DuPont for bikes.
A fireplace, a hot tub and everyone under one roof, the kind of place Mom likes.
catch: Cataloochee gets about 5 inches of natural snow in December and runs on snowmaking, so a warm spell can close it.
Snow in town is unlikely. December runs a 51-degree high and a 31-degree low.
The heated pool at Asheville 12 costs extra and isn't confirmed for winter.
Daniel would be looking at a connection or a long drive from Austin. A seasonal Allegiant nonstop isn't confirmed for December.
entry.weather: December highs around 51 and lows around 31, with snow in town unlikely. The ski areas run on snowmaking, and a warm week can shut them.

getting_there.how: Drive about 430 miles, 8 to 9 hours with stops and a three-year-old. Flying would be one stop through Charlotte to Asheville.
getting_there.est: $120 to $200 in gas per car, or $600 to $800 a seat to fly

getting_there.how: One stop through Charlotte, Atlanta or Dallas to Asheville. An Allegiant seasonal nonstop shows up on 2025 listings but isn't confirmed for December 2026.
Three family cars from Virginia, plus a rental for Daniel if he flies.

houses.name: Asheville 12 (The Top Villas)
houses.detail: Six bedrooms including a twin bunk room, five baths, sleeps 16, a hot tub, a pool that can be heated for a fee, and about 15 minutes from downtown.
houses.price: From $288 a night off-peak. Not quoted for the holiday week, where rough guesses put it at $11,000 to $20,000
houses.verdict: Worth asking about first, including any Christmas-week minimums.

houses.name: Our Mountain Retreat, Arden (south Asheville)
houses.detail: Four bedrooms in the main house plus two in a guest house, sleeps 16.
houses.verdict: Six bedrooms across two buildings on one property.

houses.name: West Asheville six-bedroom, about 6,000 square feet
houses.detail: Six bedrooms, four baths, a hot tub and a barrel sauna, sleeps 16.
houses.verdict: Another one to keep in mind, close to downtown.

agenda.all: Drive down (Virginia Beach about 8 hours, Richmond about 6). Daniel flies through Charlotte. A grocery run, the hot tub, a simple dinner at the house.
A downtown walk and lunch at Posana. The Grove Park Inn gingerbread houses in the evening (public viewing hours still to confirm).

agenda.crew: Skiing or riding at Cataloochee, about 45 minutes away.
agenda.relax: The Grove Park spa. Kids and Michael at the house.

agenda.all: Biltmore together, the house and grounds by day, then the Candlelight Christmas Evening with an early slot for the kids.
New Year's Eve chef dinner at the house.
agenda.crew: A Sugar Mountain day, about 2 hours each way, with skiing for some of us and tubing for Bennett and Taylor with an adult (age minimum still to confirm).
agenda.relax: The River Arts District and a long lunch for whoever stays.

agenda.all: A slow morning, a group hike with a view, leftovers and games.
Family photos with Patrick at golden hour.
agenda.crew: Mountain bikes at Bent Creek or DuPont, or the Cataloochee Valley elk in the Smokies.
